Power from a phone.

How the air moves

We cut a wedge out of the stove to show what the fan is doing. Blue is cool air, orange is air the stove has already heated.

  1. Power

    The cable plugs into the side. The dial at the power bank or phone end sets the fan speed.

  2. 1
    Cool air in

    The fan draws fresh air in through the slots around the base.

  3. 2
    Up the double wall

    It's pushed up the gap between the two titanium walls.

  4. 3
    Primary air

    Some of it enters low down and feeds the fire from underneath, so even damp twigs keep burning.

  5. 4
    Secondary air

    The rest heats up on its way to the top, then jets in above the flames and burns off the smoke.

  6. 5
    Heat straight up

    A hotter, cleaner flame goes straight into your pot. Over 30% efficient, with less soot.

Turn the dial, set the fire

The dial on the cable sets the fan speed. Turn it down and the fire settles to a gentle simmer. Turn it up and more air makes it burn hotter, fast enough for a rolling boil. Have a go.

Drag the dial, or tab to it and use the arrow keys.

Based on LOFI's figures: the fan draws 50 to 350mA, which gives 25 to 150 hours on a 10,000mAh power bank.

What can it burn? Almost anything dry.

Twigs, pellets, pinecones and bark are the everyday fuel. These are the ones people don't believe, so LOFI filmed them.

  • Twigs and sticks
  • Wood pellets
  • Pinecones
  • Bark
  • Paper to start it

Every part can be fixed

The base twists off on bayonet pins, so you can get to the fan and the electronics at home. Every part is sold on its own, and every stove comes with a one year warranty with free repairs.
